A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SPA-BENCH paper, with 38 complete pages including Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendering establish that pages 2–38 are identical; first-page differences concern only affiliation and version/date text.

before.justification: v2 reports original smartphone-agent evaluations in Section 6, success-detector validation in Appendices D–E, and open-ended-task experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains the original agent-performance results, success-detector validation, and open-ended-task experiments in Section 6 and Appendices D–G.

M1.justification: The agent framework, coarse-to-fine single-app evaluation, and sequential cross-app success detection are identical, including their implementation and prompting procedures in Appendices C–E.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 300 single-app and 40 cross-app tasks covering English and Chinese, plus the same ten open-ended English tasks in Appendix G. Task descriptions and application coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The same 11 agents participate in the benchmark comparisons, with AutoDroid still restricted to single-app tasks. Appendix G retains the same seven agentic-workflow comparators, and evaluator-validation comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Metrics, model configurations, evaluator settings, and testing procedures are identical. Both retain the twice-golden-steps execution limit in Appendix F.1 and the 20-step limit for open-ended tasks in Appendix G.

E4.justification: Both retain the coarse-detection ablation and reasoning/action-mode comparisons in Appendix D.3, difficulty analysis in Appendix F.3, open-ended-task analysis in Appendix G, and three case studies in Appendix H.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests; Appendix A retains the future plan to repeat experiments for robustness.

E6.justification: All numerical results, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical. For example, M3A retains a 0.640 single-app English success rate in Table 2 and a 0.700 open-ended-task success rate in Table 16; evaluator-validation results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Metric definitions and success-detection conditions are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs, and no mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: diverse smartphone tasks, a unified agent framework, and automated multidimensional evaluation. Claims about agent capabilities and deployment difficulties are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning UI grounding, memory, error handling, termination, and execution costs remain identical. Appendix A's limitations and the applicability qualifications in Appendices D–H are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware and emulator guidance, physical-device exceptions, agent adaptations, OCR processing, configurations, and prompt templates are unchanged. Project and implementation links retain the same destinations.

R1.justification: Section 2, the benchmark positioning in Table 1, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list are identical. No prior work or novelty positioning is added or removed.

P1.justification: The fourth affiliation changes from 'University College London' to 'AI Centre, University College London'. The arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 24 February 2025 to v3 dated 31 March 2025. All substantive prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–14, Tables 1–16, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–38 render identically; the first-page text updates do not reorganize its layout.

improvement.justification: v3 only specifies the AI Centre affiliation and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and all appendices remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
